newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen under pressure at the open.

* Toronto stocks were expected to open under pressure from weaker bonds and bills and unexpectedly strong U.S. retail sales but analysts saw losses limited by stronger U.S. stocks.

Toronto stocks were expected to open under pressure on Tuesday on weaker bonds and bills and unexpectedly strong U.S. retail sales data, but analysts said losses may be limited by stronger U.S. stocks.

"The bonds are already recovering from their lows after the data was released and the September S&P contract has moved from down almost two points to up. So...the U.S. market could open on the upside," said MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie.
But she said weak bonds, bills and gold prices will likely push Toronto stocks lower in early trade.
"So I think we'll open under pressure but we could close on the upside, and have a choppy day," Beattie said.
U.S. retail sales rose 0.5 percent in June after a revised 0.3 percent drop in May. Economists had predicted June sales would rise 0.2 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis.
The Toronto Stock Exchange nudged up on Monday to hit its third consecutive record close. The TSE's key 300 composite index rose 13.20 points to 6639.60.
Traders said investors are keeping an eye on corporate earnings as reporting season hits full stride this week.
"There have not been a whole lot of surprises...generally speaking I think earnings are coming in at expectations or slightly above expectations," one trader said.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---

* IPSCO Inc's second-quarter earnings jumped to C$1.11 per share from C$0.62 in 1996. The steelmaker said results were boosted by firming prices and a shorter than usual spring breakup period, which translated into unexpectedly high oil country tubular shipments in Canada.

* Placer Dome Inc said today its will report "substantially reduced" costs of gold production in the first half on 1997 compared to 1996 when results are released on July 22. The gold producer said its share of average cash production costs for the first six months of 1997 is expected to be US$214 per ounce compared with US$246 per ounce in 1996.
* Falconbridge Ltd said early today its second-quarter earnings were C$0.33 per share, unchanged from C$0.33 per share in the same period a year ago.
